title: Demand for power generation and grid equipment is booming | Wood Mackenzie
gist: GE Vernova's Roger Martella pushes back on the consensus that electrical equipment supply is the binding constraint on US electricity growth, naming permitting and grid interconnections as the more fundamental bottlenecks, while the company invests $1.3 billion and 1,800 US manufacturing jobs and targets lifting turbine capacity from 18 GW a year to 30 GW by 2030. He frames demand as diversified beyond AI - European energy security and emerging Asian growth - as a hedge against gas turbine cyclicality, treats the Darlington SMR project as a cost-learning proof point for 2030, and tells policymakers the missing ingredient is policy durability across political cycles.

insights.claim: The head of a major electrical equipment supplier rejects the widely held view that equipment supply is the main bottleneck restricting electricity supply growth, arguing permitting and grid interconnections are more fundamental difficulties for project developers.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: If true, capital and policy attention aimed at manufacturing capacity is misdirected - the alpha is in interconnection queue reform and permitting exposure, not equipment order books alone.
insights.quote: Roger rejects the idea that equipment supplies are the main bottleneck restricting electricity supply growth. Other issues, including permitting and grid interconnections, are more fundamental difficulties for project developers.

themes.theme: Demand diversification versus AI bubble risk

insights.claim: AI data center demand is one driver of GE Vernova's rapidly growing order book but not the only one, with European energy security needs and emerging Asian economic development also contributing.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Order book diversification is the key due-diligence question for equipment names - it determines how much of the backlog survives an AI capex slowdown.

insights.claim: The gas turbine market has been through boom and bust in the past, and uncertainty over the future of AI raises the question of whether the current cycle is another bubble.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Historical cyclicality is the bear case for the entire power equipment trade - size positions to survive a repeat of the previous turbine bust.
insights.quote: The gas turbine market has been through boom and bust in the past, and the uncertainty over the future of AI naturally raises the question of whether we are in another bubble today.
insights.locator: Ed raises the issue of the industry's cyclicality

insights.claim: GE Vernova's defence against cyclicality risk is that it is looking at the full range of needs driving electrification rather than making a bet solely on AI.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Management's stated hedge - verify it in segment disclosure rather than accepting it, since a diversified backlog is what separates a structural story from a bubble.
insights.quote: Roger’s answer is that the company is looking at the range of needs that are driving electrification, not making a bet solely on AI.

insights.claim: The open question for small modular reactors is whether they can move from a promising concept to a repeatable, cost-competitive business, and the answer depends on using first-of-a-kind lessons from Darlington to drive down costs for subsequent units.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: The SMR thesis is a learning-curve bet, not a technology bet - the investable signal is unit-two cost versus unit-one, not first-plant completion.

insights.so_what: A commitment framing that raises the stakes on Darlington - failure there would set back the whole SMR investment case, not just one project.

insights.claim: Skills shortages in electricians, plumbers and welders persist despite near-universal agreement that more of these skilled trades are needed to deliver infrastructure build-out, indicating the consensus diagnosis has not produced a working solution.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Labour, not steel or silicon, may cap the build rate - a persistent shortage argues for wage inflation in EPC and construction costs across power projects.
insights.quote: Just about everyone agrees that America and other countries need more electricians, plumbers and welders

insights.claim: The proposed levers for actually expanding the skilled trades workforce are pay, job security, training and the status of industrial work, and it is an open question whether these are being addressed in the right ways.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Names the four variables to watch in workforce policy; movement on pay and job security would be the earliest sign the bottleneck is easing.

insights.claim: The missing ingredient for the power sector is policy durability - frameworks that survive political cycles, court challenges and changes of administration - because industry cannot invest enough to meet long-term needs without it.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Policy volatility, not policy direction, is identified as the investment deterrent - a reason to discount capacity plans in jurisdictions with unstable frameworks.
insights.quote: the missing ingredient is policy durability. If the industry is to invest enough to meet long-term needs, it has to have policy frameworks that survive political cycles, court challenges and changes of administration
insights.locator: Roger ends with a message to policymakers

insights.claim: The equipment supplier's stated purpose is that bringing electricity to the world both raises living standards and supports decarbonization, tying grid build-out to a development case rather than a purely climate one.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: A dual-mandate framing that makes the demand story resilient to shifts in climate policy sentiment - relevant when handicapping political risk to the sector.
insights.locator: The company is driven by a sense of purpose

insights.claim: High-Voltage Direct Current transmission and cutting-edge grid management technologies including drones and AI are being discussed as part of the same equipment-demand story as turbines and transformers.

insights.so_what: Broadens the addressable market beyond generation hardware - HVDC and grid software are adjacent exposure to the same electrification capex wave.
